answer: A juniper nursery stays honest when every new identity must plant and tend a distinct juniper sapling on a different plot, watering it through one full growing season while a distinct ranger records the roots in a worn atlas at thaw. The first fake owes one sapling, the second two, the third four, doubling each time, so the tenth fake alone owes 512 saplings and twenty fakes would owe over a million. Bulk farming fails because each sapling needs a full voyage of the seasons to root, and one keeper cannot water a thousand plots before frost, like a single spade digging one hole at a time.
